chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:

"There is no objection to borrowing bread, and no objection to buying water skins and ropes, and no objection to exchanging one fals for two fals, and two qillat for [two qillat], and no objection to advance payment (salam) in coins."

key_terms.اسْتِقْرَاضُ: Borrowing or taking a loan of goods
key_terms.الرَّوَايَا: Ropes or cords used for tying and carrying
key_terms.السَّلَفُ: Advance payment contract (Salam) where payment is made before delivery of goods
key_terms.جِرَارُ: Water skins or containers for carrying water

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible forms of borrowing and advance payment (salam) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the permissibility (*ibahah*) of specific commercial practices, including *istiqrad* (borrowing staple goods), purchasing utility items, and *salam* contracts involving currency. It reflects the Shia juristic approach to facilitating trade by validating flexible debt and advance payment mechanisms, provided the underlying assets are clearly defined and deliverable.
